text:
Pittsburgh and San Jose arrive with the same 1-4-0 record over their last five. The Penguins lost 5-2 at Anaheim, where Cutter Gauthier scored three, and they're without Bryan Rust, with Tommy Novak now skating beside Crosby and Rakell. The Sharks snapped a five-game winless run by beating the Islanders in a shootout, and Michael Misa has stepped into Igor Chernyshov's spot next to Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith. Pittsburgh is also living with trade chatter around Crosby, Malkin and Rakell, per recent headlines.

The numbers favor the visitors. At five on five, PIT has taken 52% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), SJS 45%. San Jose allows 3.94 expected goals per 60 minutes, and it takes 4.5 penalties a game, though its power play (0.70 expected goals a game) is better than Pittsburgh's (0.45). In net, projected starter Sergei Murashov sits at -1.93 goals saved above expected this season, while Yaroslav Askarov is at +5.66, a reversal from his -19.4 last year. Our model has PIT at 3.56 expected goals and SJS at 3.16.

Celebrini is our top scorer pick at 46%, and he's one point from 200 career points. Smith is at 37% and one goal from 50. For Pittsburgh, Crosby (36% to score) and Malkin (71% for a point) lead the way. Among our under-the-radar picks, we like Ben Kindel at 50% for a point, well above his season pace of 37%, and Nick Robertson, whose 2.5 expected goals over his last 10 games rate better than 85% of depth forwards.
